# LDBG

> LDBG is a free falling-block RPG you play in your browser. Every line you clear hits a monster. Gather on the Farm, craft gear, fight through Greenshore and the Red Desert, and duel other players.

LDBG is a falling-block puzzle game and an RPG at once. You stack falling pieces and clear lines as in any competitive stacker, and every line you clear does something in the RPG: on the Farm it gathers materials, in a dungeon it strikes the monster in front of you, and in the Arena it hits another player. Your account keeps your character's level, gear, materials and unlocks between runs. It is made with the Godot engine by an independent developer and is in early beta.

- Play free in a desktop browser: https://play.ldbg.net/
- Official site: https://ldbg.net/
- Optional Windows app: https://github.com/redredret/redredret.github.io/releases/latest
- Controls: keyboard or controller, every action rebindable. Built for computers, not phones.
- Price: free. Guests can try a local demo; logging in keeps progress on the game's servers.

## The game in numbers

- 221 items, including 85 pieces of gear (helmets, armour, swords, bows, staves, bucklers, rings, necklaces), from 139 crafting recipes
- 30 kinds of monster, 14 of them bosses
- 2 Stories: 19 fights in Greenshore's, then 20 across the Red Desert's 6 locations
- The Endless Dungeon: 13 regions, a world map to plan trips on, and 10 pets to find
- 109 upgrades across 3 upgrade trees (Combat, Skills and Build)
- 86 quests from 8 townsfolk, and 97 daily and weekly tasks
- Live totals, read 2026-11-18: 25 adventurers, 8,357 monsters slain, 2,653 bosses slain, 3,370 Quads and 1,891 T-spins cleared, 1,690 Farm runs

## The Farm

The Farm is an endless run. Clear lines to gather logs, ore, fish and fibre, then craft with them. Quads, T-spins and combos gather more.

- **Farm Solo**: Just you and the board. Garbage rises every few pieces, so keep clearing.
- **Farm Versus**: Up to ten players in a room, sending garbage at each other. You keep everything you gather.
- **Dark Farm**: Versus with stakes. Half of what you gather is on the line, and the winner takes it.

## Crafting and gear

Smelt your ore into ingots, weave your fibre into fabric, and work them into 85 pieces of gear across 139 recipes. Everything you wear shows on your character, from helmets and armour to swords, bows, staves, bucklers, rings and necklaces. Trade the rest for Gold with other players on the Market.

## Dungeons

Greenshore's story runs 19 fights long, from zombies on the shore to the Cult Leader at the top of the tower. Beat him and the Red Desert opens: 20 more fights across 6 places, from the Dust Bowl to the cult's dig at the Research Station, and through the gate they guard to the Unbound in the Hellish Desert. Your lines are your attacks. Theirs land on your board: arrows knock out blocks, fire spreads along the bottom row, a worm chomps your tower and a mummy binds your HOLD shut.

- **Story**: Two set routes, through every area and every boss: Greenshore's first, then the Red Desert's.
- **The Endless Dungeon**: 13 regions, from Greenshore's fields to the Hellish Desert. The desert's open once you have finished its Story. Plan a trip place by place on the world map, or just wander. The deeper you go, the better the chests.
- **With a Friend**: Take a friend into the Endless Dungeon. You fight the same monster, share every kill, and can pick each other up when one of you goes down.
- **Dark Endless**: DANGER. A riskier, more rewarding endless dungeon. Fight other players for their gear, and higher monster drop rates, while risking your gear.
- **The Garbage Man**: 10 waves of garbage, faster every wave. One top-out ends it.
- **The Slime King**: A king after every king, alone or with a friend. He walls your board down to four columns until he falls. A Slime Key opens his door.

## Bosses

- **Bandit King**: Switches between arrow rain and a blade spin that cuts your top and bottom rows.
- **Cyclops**: Knocks blocks loose from the top of your stack, then sets it on fire.
- **Punchy**: Slams the ground, and a stone wave sweeps across one of your rows.
- **Shooty**: Hurls boulders that drop three or four stone blocks onto your board.
- **Bernie**: A fire-casting cyclops whose fireball spreads along your bottom row.
- **Cult Leader**: Opens portals and hurls fireballs, then shields itself from your next hit.
- **The Garbage Man**: Throws garbage at you one line at a time, faster every wave. Beat wave ten for an Arcane Vault, then keep going.
- **The Slime King**: Walls your board down to four columns, slimes your tower and wraps you up until you shake him off. Beat him and a bigger one comes for you.
- **Desert Worm**: Swims through the air, chomps blocks out of your tower to heal itself, then burrows through it. Only a clear across its trail can hit it down there.
- **Scrap Warlord**: Pays his crew to shoot your board, then spins into a dust devil that rips at the sides of your tower until you hit him.
- **Possessed Sarcophagus**: Seals your deepest well with a stone, lets spirits loose on your tower, and raises the dead to take your hits for it.
- **Sandstone Golem**: Cracks your stack, blinds your queue with dust and makes your pieces heavy. Clear his crack or T-spin into his gap to stun him.
- **The Old Man**: The Sand Veil keep him chained at the bottom of their dig. They have studied him for years and never let him die. He does not fight back.
- **The Unbound**: What came through the gate. He lights a ward on your stack to fill, rewrites the pieces coming, and demands three clears in a row. Miss it and a row of hell-iron rises that takes two clears to break.

## Lesser foes

- **Zombie**: Swipes a block off your top.
- **Super Zombie**: Rakes off two or three.
- **Slime**: Slimes your piece. No rotating.
- **Squirrel**: Nips at you. Never your board.
- **Bandit**: Arrows knock out a block.
- **Bandit Elite**: A tougher bandit, crossbow and all.
- **Cultist**: Fireballs, and a stab at your bottom row.
- **Oak Entling**: A stump that refused to stay felled.
- **Sand Zombie**: Swipes a block off your top, twice as hard.
- **Wormling**: Bites off a block and heals on it.
- **Raider**: Slashes a block off your top.
- **Mummy**: Binds your HOLD shut until you hit it twice.
- **Rockling**: Heaves stones onto your tallest column.
- **Cave Spider**: Lays an egg on your stack. Clear it before it hatches.
- **Sand Veil Cultist**: Brands blocks to flare unless you clear them.
- **Lesser Cult Leader**: Sun portals, a ring of blocks, and a shield only a spin breaks.

## The Arena

In the Hollow Spire you pick your opponent off the board. Look over their gear first, then fight for the win, or put a piece of your gear against a piece of theirs. Every hit you land is a line you cleared, so the better stacker usually walks away richer.

## Questions

### What is LDBG?

LDBG is a free falling-block RPG you play in your browser. Every line you clear is an attack on the monster in front of you. You gather materials on the Farm, craft gear, fight through two Stories, Greenshore and the Red Desert, push on into the Endless Dungeon, and duel other players, and your account keeps your levels, gear and loot.

### Is LDBG free to play?

Yes. LDBG is free and plays in your browser at play.ldbg.net. Try it as a guest, or Log In so everything you earn is kept.

### Do I need to download anything?

No. It runs in a desktop browser such as Chrome, Edge or Firefox. There is also an optional Windows app that opens the same game in its own window, with extra settings like higher frame rates; it isn't signed yet, so Windows asks you to confirm before it runs.

### What do I play it with?

A keyboard or a controller, on a computer. Every control can be rebound in Settings, and handling such as auto-repeat and soft drop speed can be tuned the way competitive stackers like it.

### Can I play on my phone?

Not yet. LDBG needs a keyboard or a controller, so play it on a computer. Touch controls are planned.

### How does the RPG side work?

Clearing lines gathers logs, ore, fish and fibre on the Farm, or deals damage in a dungeon. Bigger clears hit harder: Quads, T-spins and combos all pay extra. You earn XP and levels, spend points across 3 upgrade trees, craft gear and improve it at the Forge, finish quests, daily tasks and bounties, find pets, and open reward chests.

### Can I play with friends?

Yes. Farm Versus seats up to ten players who send garbage at each other, Dark Farm puts half your haul on the line, the Endless Dungeon and the Slime King can be fought with a friend, and the Arena lets you duel another player for the win or for each other's gear. Add your friends in the game to see when they are on and invite them straight in.

### Is my progress saved?

Yes. When you Log In, your progress is kept on the game's servers and follows you to any computer, and it stays through the beta: nothing you earn now will be wiped. Guest play is a short local demo, and nothing earned as a guest moves to an account.

### Is LDBG finished?

No, it is in early beta and grows every week. New dungeons, bosses, gear and modes land often; the Recently Added list on this page shows the latest.

## Recently added

- 2026-11-18, **Fairer duels**: Thorns no longer win fights on their own: in a duel, Thorned and the Ring of Thorns hand back a small share that adds up over the fight. Heals were made for monsters, so in a duel Mending heals an eighth, and Vampiric, the Hourglass Amulet and the Combat tree's heals count at half. Dark now looks for an opponent within ten levels, in your own region first, then your part of the world, then anywhere.
- 2026-11-18, **The Red Desert's Story, told in full**: The Red Desert's Story has a new opening and a new ending. Vesper joins Katherine and Brann on the road in, and once the Unbound falls and the portal goes quiet, stay to hear what became of the Old Man, and what the cultists are really after. You get a few words of your own, too.
- 2026-11-17, **Rook's hunts and diaries reach the end of the desert**: Rook can now send you after Sand Veil Cultists in the Research Station, and those kills count toward Greenshore's Cultists too, or after the Unbound himself in the Hellish Desert. The Research Station and the Hellish Desert have diaries of their own, Easy to Elite, with a badge each; their diaries pay Blank Charts. And the Desert Orb now needs a fifth soul: the Lesser Cult Leader's, along with the four desert bosses. The Unbound's soul is not wanted.
- 2026-11-17, **Desert Master, and the desert cult's idols**: A new Feat, Desert Master: kill the Unbound ten times in the Dark Endless Dungeon, and every cultist takes 10% more damage from you, the Sand Veil and their leader as well as Greenshore's. With Greenshore Master too, Greenshore's cultists take 20% more. And the Sand Veil Cultist and the Lesser Cult Leader can now drop the Cult Idol, as Greenshore's cultists do. Runs you started before this keep the old rules.
- 2026-11-17, **New quests across the Red Desert**: Katherine has a new quest line, Across the Sand: follow the trouble into the Red Desert one boss at a time, from the Desert Worm to the Unbound, for adamantite and then orichalcum gear. Vesper's road goes three steps deeper, into the desert regions of the Endless Dungeon and out of its Dark alive, and Maeve has rewards waiting at levels 45, 50, 55 and 60. Three new quest lines teach the desert's later bosses: Vesper on breaking the Sandstone Golem's stone, Katherine on the Sand Veil's sun magic, and Brann on meeting the Unbound's Demands. And the Red Desert's Story now opens with a scene of its own.
- 2026-11-17, **Bounties, diaries and tasks in the Red Desert**: Rook has work in the Red Desert now. Once a desert region has joined your Endless Dungeon, his board can ask for Sand Zombies, Worms, Raiders, Mummies, Rocklings or Cave Spiders, or for the Desert Worm, the Scrap Warlord, the Possessed Sarcophagus or the Sandstone Golem themselves. The Desert Worm counts toward Worms, the Warlord toward his Raiders and the Golem toward Rocklings. Marked desert champions drop trophies of their own, and every trophy is now traded to Rook for Marks straight from your bag: open it and press TRADE. The Dust Bowl, the Sand Storm, the Pyramids and the Sand Cave each have a diary, Easy to Elite, with a badge, and there are new daily and weekly tasks for the desert. The tougher ones pay better chests, and finishing the desert Story pays an Arcane Vault.
- 2026-11-17, **The Unbound ends the Red Desert**: The Red Desert's Story has a new last fight. When the Old Man falls, the Research Station turns to hell and the Unbound comes through the gate. He lights a ward on your stack to fill, brands two rows to clear in one go, rewrites the pieces coming, and demands three clears in a row. Miss his demand and a row of hell-iron rises under your stack that takes two clears to break. Beat him to finish the Story, and two new places open in the Endless Dungeon: the Research Station, where the Lesser Cult Leader holds the dig, and the Hellish Desert, where every fight is the Unbound. Runs you started before this end on the Old Man.
- 2026-11-17, **Brann's quest: The Ancient Mask**: Brann has noticed something odd about the Mummies in the Red Desert: they seem to be guarding something. Keep killing them until one drops the Desert Orb. It's an old artifact that loses its power over time, so it has to be charged in one trip: put it in your new QUEST slot and take the souls of all four desert bosses in a single Endless or Dark run, alone or with a friend. The orb glows brighter with every boss. Bring it back to Brann and he lets you use his master's forge, which teaches you the Ancient Mask and the Ancient Warhelm.
